name: Diodio
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: SIL PNG and OLAC unreachable; no confirmed phonology or grammar of Diodio located.

sources.citation: Wikipedia contributors. 'Diodio language', en.wikipedia.org, wikitext downloaded 2026-09-17.
Gibson, Stan. 1992. Bwaidoka organised phonology data. Ukarumpa: SIL-PNG.
sources.note: Not Diodio (bwai1242), but the closest modern phonological description in the same Goodenough dialect chain; a stress statement there would be the nearest proxy and would flag what to expect for Diodio. SIL sites are could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Monieta, Polikap (ed.); Marcela Vargas & Denis Vargas (SIL facilitators). 2018. Molata meȳa ana vaiyawawa / Trial spelling guide for the Molata language. Uwauwefo, MBP: SIL-PNG. 22 pp. (SIL archive 79367; Alphabet Development Workshop 9-13 April 2018)
sources.note: Alphabet and spelling rules only (consonants incl. bw, mw, nw, kw, fw, lw, ȳ; five vowels; 'We write double vowels to indicate that we pull them (it is a long sound): faa, boo, aa'; words never end in a consonant). No mention of stress or accent anywhere.

sources.citation: Callister, Sandra (consultant); Mariela Del Pozzi & Marcia de Goes (facilitators). 2017. Buki ifuifufu wona Molata / Stories in the Molata language. Trial edition. Alotau: SIL-PNG. 28 pp. (SIL archive 79410)
sources.note: Writers'-workshop story booklet; one page 'Molata alphabet' (consonant and vowel letters with sample words). Nothing on stress. Confirms Molata is 'the most spoken dialect of the West Goodenough language' (about 3000 speakers).

sources.citation: OLAC. 'OLAC resources in and about the West Goodenough language' [ddi], language-archives.org, snapshot 2026-02-18 (via the Internet Archive); plus SIL Language & Culture Archives listing for ddi (2015 snapshot) and entry pages 50141, 79367, 79410
sources.note: Catalogue only. The complete OLAC holdings for ddi are: Ross 1980 'Diodio (wordlist, sentences)' PARADISEC MR1-020; Glottolog; Ethnologue; the 2017 Molata stories; the 2018 Molata spelling guide. No phonology, grammar or Organised Phonology Data for Diodio exists in SIL's archive or OLAC.

sources.citation: Kassell, Alison & Philip Lambrecht. 2012. A sociolinguistic profile of the West and North Goodenough groups. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2012-024. Dallas: SIL International. 53 pp. (Glottolog 313196)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sociolinguistic survey (dialect boundaries, vitality) with 190-item wordlists in broad IPA for Molata/Giwau/Miyalabi villages (Appendix E, pp. 40-53) with no stress marks; Appendix B gives tables of possible consonant and vowel phones (pp. 38-39) and one footnote uses 'accent' only in the dialect sense (p. 14 n.a). Section 1.3 lists all prior work: Lithgow & Staalsen 1965, Huckett 1981 (Iduna), Gibson & Spaeth 1993 'Diodio survey report' (ms.).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2009. Change request 2009-030 [ddi], submitted by Sara Van Cott (SIL-PNG), adopted 2010-01-18. 5 pp. (Glottolog 500839)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Renames ddi 'West Goodenough'; states all Goodenough dialects except Kaninuwa form a dialect chain, speakers use the names Molata, Miyalabi or Giwau, and 'Diodio' is a ward name; sole source cited is Kassell & Lambrecht (then 'to appear').

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of Western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU. (Glottolog 98107)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Diodio appears in reflex lists and the Papuan Tip consonant-correspondence tables (ch. 6) and in the sources appendix (data: SIL; informant John Manasa of Diodio, pp. 400, 408). No statement on Diodio stress.

sources.citation: Lithgow, David R. 1976. Austronesian languages: Milne Bay and adjacent islands (Milne Bay Province). In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2, 441-523. Pacific Linguistics C-39.
sources.note: §16 (p. 453) locates Diodio (Awale, Molata, Diodio, Utalo, Yauyaula wards) and gives Lithgow & Staalsen 1965 dialect percentages; §84 'Stress' (p. 475) is a Papuan-Tip-cluster-level remark only ('In all of the languages of PTC it seems that stress is predictable within certain word-classes, notably kinship nouns and verbs'; stress phonemic in Kilivila, Muyuw, Budibud, Misima) — Diodio is not named and no placement rule is given.

sources.citation: Gibson, Stan & David Spaeth. 1993. Diodio survey report. Manuscript, SIL-PNG Survey Office, Ukarumpa.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other Diodio-specific document known; Gibson wrote the Bwaidoka Organised Phonology Data (1992) and may have noted stress in the Diodio wordlist he took. Unpublished manuscript.

sources.citation: Huckett, Joyce. 1981. Dialects of the Iduna language. Manuscript, SIL Ukarumpa; and Huckett's Iduna phonology/grammar papers (Glottolog idun1242)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Iduna (viv) is the adjoining member of the Goodenough dialect chain; an Iduna stress rule would be the nearest published proxy but must not be entered under diod1237.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm (collector). 1980. Diodio (wordlist B, sentences). PARADISEC MR1-020 (3 scanned notebook pages, audio side A)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only linguist-collected primary record of Diodio; Ross's field wordlists sometimes mark stress on the transcriptions, and the audio would allow a check. Login-gated and could not be reached by automated download.
